chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meaning of the statement of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) when he looked at the second person who was wrapped in his garment: 'No one is more beloved to me than that I meet Allah with a scroll like this wrapped one.' He said: 'By it, I mean the scroll that was written in the Kaaba.'

key_terms.صَحِيفَة: Scroll or sheet of paper, metaphorically used here for the body/record of deeds

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali mean when he referred to a wrapped companion as a 'scroll'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) declaration of love for a companion wrapped in his garment, interpreting the 'scroll' (sahifa) not as a physical document but as the companion’s own body, which serves as a record of deeds inscribed by God. This metaphor highlights the concept of the human form as a living testament to faith and divine decree, a theme deeply resonant in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt and their companions. The reference to the Kaaba underscores the sanctity of this 'scroll,' linking the physical vessel to the holiest site in Islam, thereby elevating the companion's status to one of divine proximity.
